title: Ice ages

data.source: LR04 benthic oxygen-18 stack, Lisiecki and Raymo (2005), last 800,000 years

prediction: In the younger 400,000 years, forecasting each termination from the time the ice first reaches a level learned on the older 400,000 years has lower RMSE than a fixed clock learned on the same older half.
baseline: A fixed clock: last termination plus the mean gap of the older half. (The field's threshold models are the count idea already.)
why: Waiting for the ice to reach a level forecast the terminations better than a fixed clock. But ice-volume threshold models are already the standard account of the ice ages. The result is also fragile: it rests on five terminations, it flips when only the largest swings are counted, and the count forecast is made later in the cycle than the clock forecast.
